topics.topic: Backup snapshot interaction with concurrent live Registry transactions, including room creation
questions: Does A21’s concurrency review cover M03 and concurrent room creation during a backup, or is the affected-model list intentionally exhaustive and excluding it?

When a backup snapshot and a live Registry transaction contend for the store, which operation waits or retries, and may either the backup run or the caller's operation fail because of that contention?

quotes:
A backup is a consistent copy of the store taken while Registry runs:
one snapshot of the store, as one read transaction sees it, while other
transactions go on; it never holds part of a transaction, and its
recorded instant and last sequence number are those of that snapshot,
the instant being when its read transaction began.

concurrency: APPLICABLE; references: A01, A04, A07, A12, A13, A14, A16, A18; affected: M01, M04, M05, M06, M09, M10, M11, concurrent creates, corrections, publishes, session changes, single-use confirmation values, confirmations bound to no revision, resubmitted forms on records without a revision, creates racing the erasure that removes their request id, re-uploads replacing a confirmed file, concurrent import confirmations, backup snapshots taken while transactions go on, overlapping backup runs
Registry keeps serving, and the next 03:00 tries again.
judgement.divergence: One implementation waits or retries when the backup read snapshot contends with a live write, allowing the room creation and then keeping the backup; another fails that day's backup on contention while the room creation succeeds. The owner notices the different newest-backup state. The omission of M03 from A21 does not itself change room behavior because the snapshot covers the whole store, but the contention outcome remains open.
judgement.why: The texts require one consistent snapshot while transactions continue but do not decide whether lock contention waits, retries, or fails the backup or live operation.

witness.initial: Registry is serving with an active project, no room R, no kept backup for the date, and the daily run is due.
events: Cabinet Kernel for a registered, granted agent session starts adding room R and its store transaction remains open.
Registry's backup scheduler starts the daily run and attempts to begin the read transaction defining the snapshot while the room transaction contends with it.
outcomes: Registry waits or retries; the room transaction commits and the run keeps a consistent backup.
Registry treats snapshot contention as a backup failure; the room transaction commits but no backup is kept for that date and no ordinary retry occurs before the next eligible 03:00.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether the newest kept backup advances.
basis: | add a room | owner; Cabinet Kernel for the agent, on a project its session is granted (R0-41, R0-46) | the room: an identity Registry mints, the given name, its project (R0-10) | missing name refused; unknown or archived project refused; a second room of the same name is a second room (R0-10); a project the session is not granted refused |

Every day at
03:00 UTC, while Registry runs with its service tokens, it
makes one backup run; a 03:00 that finds Registry stopped, or in an
owner-only start (rule 9), makes no run, and none is made later in its
place.

A backup is a consistent copy of the store taken while Registry runs:
one snapshot of the store, as one read transaction sees it, while other
transactions go on; it never holds part of a transaction, and its
recorded instant and last sequence number are those of that snapshot,
the instant being when its read transaction began.

topics.topic: Required evidence verifying that backup runs do not overlap
questions: What required evidence verifies the non-overlap property on which the changed concurrency review relies?

topics.topic: Scope and enforcement boundary for mutually exclusive backup runs
questions: Across what boundary must backup runs be mutually exclusive, and what happens if two valid Registry processes or instances use the same backup location?

quotes:
A run starts when an earlier look of this
process saw this date before 03:00, the look is at or after 03:00, this
process did not run this date, no run is going, and no kept backup of the
date exists — a file whose record cannot be read counting as none (A18
rule 1).

Every regular file directly in the location
whose name begins with the temporary prefix of
`capability:release_declarations.backup_name_prefixes` is removed; a
failed removal stops the run (A18 rule 4).
judgement.why: The later flow makes non-overlap process-local; two processes sharing a location may both run, and each run removes every matching temporary file there, including one created by the other process.
